# Weathering and Erosion

Weathering is the breakdown of rock in place, while erosion is the
transport of that broken material by wind, water, or ice.

Why does mechanical weathering dominate in cold climates? Because
freeze-thaw cycles repeatedly expand water trapped in rock cracks,
prying them apart faster than chemical processes can act.

## Key Terms

Frost wedging: the splitting of rock caused by the expansion of freezing
water in cracks.
Oxidation: a chemical weathering process also known as rusting when it
affects iron-rich minerals.
Exfoliation: the peeling away of rock layers, sometimes known as
sheeting.

## Comparing Weathering Types

Chemical weathering breaks down rock through reactions such as oxidation
and dissolution, however mechanical weathering breaks rock apart
physically without changing its composition. For example, acid rain
dissolving limestone illustrates the relationship between water
chemistry and rock decomposition.
